title: The Crisis of the Third Century
objective: After this level you can explain the chaos of the third century, when emperors rose and fell rapidly.
summary: From 235 to 284 CE, more than 20 emperors came and went, an emperor was captured, and the empire split in three before Aurelian reunited it.

cards.headline: More than 20 emperors in about 50 years. Most of them were murdered.
cards.body: Remember 69 CE, when the legions learned they could make and unmake emperors? For half a century, they did it again and again. Becoming emperor was a promotion with a very short life expectancy.

cards.headline: Everything at once
cards.body: From 235 to 284 CE, the Crisis of the Third Century, the empire suffered civil wars, invasions, plague and economic trouble, all at the same time. Even the money went bad. Emperors had kept reducing the silver in the denarius until the coin held very little, and prices soared. Imagine every new batch of coins holding a little less of the metal that made them worth anything. That was Roman money in the third century.

cards.headline: An emperor taken prisoner
cards.body: Then came the low point. In 260 CE the emperor Valerian was captured by the Persian king Shapur I. No Roman emperor had ever been taken prisoner by a foreign enemy before. The empire itself came apart, too. For a time it split into three: a breakaway Gallic Empire in the west, Rome in the middle, and Palmyra under Queen Zenobia in the east. One empire, three maps.

cards.fact: Aurelian put the pieces back together.
cards.context: In the 270s the emperor Aurelian reunited the three pieces into one empire. He also built new walls around Rome itself. A reunited empire whose capital needed fresh walls: that is the third century in a single picture.

cards.headline: The crisis: survived
learned: The crisis ran from 235 to 284 CE

questions.prompt: Which emperor was captured by the Persians in 260 CE?
questions.explanation: Valerian was captured by Shapur I, the first emperor taken prisoner by a foreign enemy.

questions.prompt: Why did prices soar during the crisis?

options.label: Coins held less and less silver

questions.explanation: Emperors cut the silver in the denarius, so each coin was worth less and prices rose.

questions.prompt: From Level 55: what had 69 CE revealed that the third century showed again?

options.label: Emperors had to be born in Rome
Armies could make and unmake emperors

questions.explanation: In both periods, armies raised their own commanders to the throne and removed others.
